title: How to turn website traffic into demos without a form
summary: Demo forms lose buyers to friction and waiting. Compare scheduling, tours, chat and AI demo agents, then set up a form-free demo step by step.
body_markdown:
To turn website traffic into demos without a form, put the demo on the page: let the visitor start it with one click (or one email field), see the product right away, and book a rep only if they want one. Karumi does this with an AI demo agent that shows your real product live on your website, so the visitor gets the demo in seconds instead of a form and a calendar invite.


Karumi is an AI demo agent: an autonomous agent that shows a buyer your real product live, by voice or chat, and answers questions as it goes. It is one of several ways to remove the form. This guide compares all of them, with sources, prices where they are public, and a setup plan you can follow this quarter.


## Why do demo request forms lose buyers?


A demo request form asks for effort first and gives value later. Buyers pay twice: once to fill it in, and again to wait for the meeting.


**Many people who start a form never finish it.** Zuko's benchmark of 739 forms puts the average starter-to-completion rate at 51.7% ([Zuko form statistics](https://www.zuko.io/form-statistics) , checked November 2026). On average, about half of the people who start typing never press submit.


**The wait after the form costs more.** In an audit of 2,241 US companies published in Harvard Business Review, firms that replied to a web lead within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify it as firms that waited longer. The average reply took 42 hours ([HBR, The Short Life of Online Sales Leads](https://hbr.org/2011/03/the-short-life-of-online-sales-leads) ). The study is old, but the pattern still holds: interest fades fast. We cover the cost in detail in[the cost of the demo wait](https://karumi.ai/blog/cost-of-demo-wait) .


**Not every request becomes a meeting.** RevenueHero puts the median rate from qualified demo request to booked meeting at 62% ([RevenueHero benchmarks](https://www.revenuehero.io/blog/demo-request-to-booked-conversion-rate-benchmarks-in-2026) , checked November 2026). The rest are lost to routing, scheduling and no-shows.


**Buyers do not want the call yet.** Gartner surveyed 646 B2B buyers and found that 67% prefer a rep-free experience, and 45% used AI during a recent purchase ([Gartner, March 2026](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-03-09-gartner-sales-survey-finds-67-percent-of-b2b-buyers-prefer-a-rep-free-experience) ). A form that only leads to a sales call asks for the one thing most buyers want to delay.


For the wider shift, read[why SaaS companies are replacing demo request forms](https://karumi.ai/blog/why-saas-companies-are-replacing-demo-request-forms) .


## What are the options to replace a demo request form?


There are five common options in 2026. They solve different parts of the problem.


1. **Instant scheduling.** The form stays, but a calendar opens the moment the visitor submits. This removes the reply wait, not the form or the meeting wait.
2. **Interactive product tours.** The visitor clicks through a captured copy of your product, with no form. Tours are fast to ship, but they follow a fixed click-path and cannot answer questions.
3. **AI chat on the website.** A chat assistant answers questions, qualifies the visitor and offers a meeting. It explains the product but usually does not show it.
4. **Free trial or sandbox.** The visitor uses the product alone. This works for simple products and for buyers who like to explore. Complex products often stall at setup.
5. **AI demo agent.** An agent opens the real product, shows it live and talks with the visitor, by voice or chat. It answers questions, adapts to the visitor and routes them to the right next step at the end.


You can combine them. A common pattern is chat first, then a live demo when intent is clear, then a booked meeting for the visitors who qualify.

## How do you set up a form-free demo on your website?


Here is a setup plan for any of the options above. Steps 4 and 5 assume an AI demo agent, but most of the plan applies to tours and chat too.


1. **Pick the pages with demo intent.** Start where buyers already ask for a demo: the homepage hero, the pricing page, the "Book a demo" page and comparison pages.
2. **Cut the form to one field, or none.** Ask for a work email at most. Karumi's own website demo asks for an email and learns everything else in the conversation ([karumi.ai/website-demo](https://karumi.ai/website-demo) ). Company, size and role can come from enrichment or from the talk itself.
3. **Make the first step instant.** The visitor should see the product within seconds of the click. On the Karumi website demo, the agent joins a live call in under two seconds and shares its screen. If your option needs a wait, say how long.
4. **Choose what the demo covers.** List the workflows buyers ask about most, and the questions that block a purchase (pricing, integrations, security). An autonomous agent picks from these during the demo, based on what each visitor says.
5. **Define every ending.** Decide what happens after the demo: book a meeting with the right rep, start a trial or subscription, or close politely for visitors who do not fit (students, competitors, out-of-region). Connect your calendar and your CRM so the session, the transcript and the next step land in HubSpot or Salesforce.
6. **Keep a human path visible.** Leave a "Talk to sales" link next to the demo. Some buyers want a person, and they should not need to fight the page to reach one.
7. **Run it against your form.** Send part of the traffic to the old form and part to the new demo for four to six weeks. Compare the metrics below, not page views.


In our experience, visitors ask about pricing, integrations and fit for their team early in a demo. Plan for those three topics before anything else.


## What should you measure?


A form-free demo changes the funnel, so the old "form fills" metric no longer fits. Track these instead:


Metric What it tells you


Demo start rate Share of page visitors who start the demo. Compare it with your old form completion rate.


Time to first demo Minutes from first visit to seeing the product. A form plus calendar is often days.


Engaged time and questions asked Whether visitors stayed and what they wanted to know.


Qualified share Share of demo sessions that match your ideal customer profile.


Meetings booked and held Whether the demo leads to sales conversations, and whether people show up.


Pipeline per 1,000 visitors The final test. It accounts for both volume and quality.


Also read the questions. What buyers ask in a demo is direct input for your website copy, your sales deck and your FAQ. Karumi records every session with analytics and conversion events, so marketing can see what visitors asked before they left.


## Which option should you pick?


Pick based on your product and your traffic:


- **Simple product, low price:** a free trial plus an interactive tour is often enough.
- **Good form traffic, slow follow-up:** add instant scheduling first. It is the smallest change.
- **Many questions before purchase:** add AI chat on pricing and FAQ pages.
- **Complex product, high-intent traffic, sales team at capacity:** an AI demo agent gives every visitor a real demo without adding headcount. ## FAQ


### Can I really get rid of the demo request form?


For most visitors, yes. Let them start the demo with one click or one email field, and keep a short booking step at the end for the people who want a rep. The form stops being the entry point and becomes an optional last step.


### Will I lose lead data without a form?


Usually not. An email field plus enrichment covers company and size. A conversation captures more than a form does: the use case, the team, the timeline and the objections, in the buyer's own words. Karumi syncs this to HubSpot, Salesforce and Attio.


### What is the best interactive product demo software to replace a B2B demo request form?


It depends on what the form did for you. If the form mainly booked meetings, instant scheduling tools such as Chili Piper fit. If buyers mainly wanted to see the product, an interactive tour tool such as Navattic or Storylane works for simple flows. If buyers need questions answered on the real product, an AI demo agent such as Karumi replaces both the form and the first sales call.


### How is an AI demo agent different from an interactive tour?


A tour is a captured copy of your product with a fixed click-path. An AI demo agent works in the real product, decides what to show based on what the buyer says, and answers questions by voice or chat. Read[what an AI demo agent is](https://karumi.ai/blog/what-is-an-ai-demo-agent) for more detail.


### Does a form-free demo work for enterprise buyers?


Yes, as a first step. Enterprise buyers still need calls, security reviews and procurement. A demo on the website lets a buyer check fit before the first call, so the first meeting starts further along. Karumi's Enterprise plan includes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and GDPR, according to[Karumi pricing](https://karumi.ai/pricing) .


### How long does setup take?


Instant scheduling and tours can go live in days. An AI demo agent needs access to your product and a list of the workflows to show. Most teams start with a pilot on one use case, measure it, then expand.


### What if visitors want to talk to a person?


Keep a "Talk to sales" link next to the demo. An AI demo agent can also book the meeting with the right rep at the end of the session, with the full context already in your CRM.
